quest.title: Mending Painting Prospects
quest.description: Batlo from Mondstadt appears to have something on his mind...

dialogues.speaker: Batlo
dialogues.text: The next painting is... Right. It's this one...

dialogues.speaker: Batlo
dialogues.text: I heard so much about you from my colleagues and was wondering if you would grace this grand event.

dialogues.speaker: Batlo
dialogues.text: And as luck would have it, here you are! It is truly an honor to meet you!

dialogues.speaker: Batlo
dialogues.text: There are many things I wish to introduce to you, but before that, allow me to introduce myself.

dialogues.speaker: Batlo
dialogues.text: I am Batlo, a painter... You should be quite familiar with this profession, no?

dialogues.speaker: Batlo
dialogues.text: But in addition to being a painter myself, I am also an art conservator.

dialogues.speaker: Batlo
dialogues.text: No matter what type of damage a painting has suffered, whether it was burnt, chewed on by rodents, rotted by mold, or any similar matter...

dialogues.speaker: Batlo
dialogues.text: As long as it is in my hands, I can restore the painting to its original, most perfect state!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Restoring paintings... Do you just repaint them?

dialogues.speaker: Batlo
dialogues.text: Hahaha! Of course not. Were I to just repaint them exactly as they were, that would be called "copying."

dialogues.speaker: Batlo
dialogues.text: What we art conservators must do is restore a piece of artwork to its most original pristine condition.

dialogues.speaker: Batlo
dialogues.text: Every detail, from the colors to the brushstrokes... Even the material of the canvas itself must be exactly the same as the original painting.

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: Isn't it? It takes exceptional painting skill, as well as uncommonly keen and detailed image perception.

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: Which is why... I simply haven't been able to hire many capable assistants.

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: I mean, if a painter has both exceptional skills and a keen perception of the smallest details...

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: Then why not just focus on their own work instead of helping restore that of other artists?

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: Not to mention how this job doesn't pay well, and how people often think of us as a bunch of copycats with mediocre skills...

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: But every job needs to be done by someone, wouldn't you agree?

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: Art is a precious thing. An outstanding painting can carry history, stories, and emotions... and of course its market value.

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: No matter what others think, as an artist myself, I will not stand idly by and watch those paintings deteriorate.

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: But... as I just said, this job doesn't pay well, and is often misunderstood.

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: Though I've been busy trying to recruit assistants, as you can see, as of now I'm still the only one doing the job.

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: That's why I'm here today. I want to educate people about what an art conservator does, and perhaps I'll be able to recruit a few more people this way.

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: However... Though I've yet to find an assistant, I have received numerous commissions to restore ancient paintings.

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: These old paintings come from Mondstadt and Liyue. They include landscapes, figures, animals, and even... crayon drawings from children...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You restore crayon drawings, too?

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: Uh... In principle, as long as it's a painting, it's a valid commission.

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: Besides, even a child's crayon drawing contains the hard work they poured into it. Who is to say it may not be their first step to becoming an artist one day?

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: So, it's understandable that their parents would come to me for to restore it.

choices.text: Your expression says you haven't even managed to convince yourself...

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: What? No! Not at all! I am absolutely not exasperated by these sorts of requests... I just have to study crayon drawings a bit...

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, if you could, would you be willing to do me a favor?

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: As you can see, I'm the only one here... But to restore a painting, I need to go out and find the relevant scenery painted therein...

choices.text: You need to go out and find the original scenery?

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: Alas, indeed! Not only that, I also have to do all kinds of research on materials relevant to the painting.

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: For example, how the scenery and animals depicted looked like at the time they were painted...

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: Fortunately, the paintings I'm currently commissioned to restore aren't too old, so things shouldn't have changed drastically.

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: I was about to head out to study the original locations, but as you know... the wilderness is a dangerous place for those more adept with the brush than the sword...

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: That's why I'd like to ask you to find the relevant scenery for me.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm not artistically gifted...

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: No worries! I have already prepared everything that you'll need... I've done this before when hiring others to help me in the past...

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: Look! This is a photo of the painting to be restored, and I have already marked the key landmarks in it.

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: All you need to do is to find the location and take photos of the marked objects with this Kamera, and you're done!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So... I just need to take photos?

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: That's right, but you ought to familiarize yourself with the paintings before taking the picture.

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: You need to feel their aesthetics and artistic sense... Let the paintings linger in your mind.

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: As long as you understand them, perhaps you'll be able to sense the entire process of how these paintings were done while taking photos.

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: Sketching, outlining, coloring, refining the details...

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: You are correct. To me, art... is a type of hallucination...

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: What an artist must do is capture the hallucination in detail and express it objectively.

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: Believe me, just study the photos I give you, and you will surely feel the "artistic hallucinations" within.

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: #I entrust this task to you, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: And I... shall start on restoring these paintings... Right. The next one is...

choices.text: Hallucinating it does seem a bit much...
That's quite a lot of preparation.
Do you know how to do crayon drawings?

response.speaker: Batlo
response.text: S—Sure! I'm just not an expert crayon artist, and I'm only superficially familiar with the literature. So I must study up on knowledge regarding crayon drawings!
